books.section: Unit 5: Toward the Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877)

primary_sources: “Caution!! Colored people of Boston, one & all,” broadside, April 24, 1851

stimulus.source_note: “Caution!! Colored people of Boston, one & all,” broadside posted in Boston, April 24, 1851 (Library of Congress, Printed Ephemera Collection). Public domain.
stimulus.text: Caution!! Colored people of Boston, one & all, You are hereby respectfully cautioned and advised, to avoid conversing with the Watchmen and Police Officers of Boston, For since the recent Order of the Mayor & Aldermen, they are empowered to act as Kidnappers and Slave Catchers, And they have already been actually employed in Kidnapping, Catching, and Keeping Slaves. Therefore, if you value your Liberty, and the Welfare of the Fugitives among you, Shun them in every possible manner, as so many Hounds on the track of the most unfortunate of your race. Keep a Sharp Look Out for Kidnappers, and have Top Eye open. April 24, 1851.

source: original; stimulus as noted in stimulus.source_note
stem: According to the broadside, why should Black Bostonians avoid talking with Boston's watchmen and police officers?

options.text: The officers had joined the abolitionist movement.
options.misconception: The broadside says the opposite: the officers had become slave catchers, not abolitionists.

options.text: The officers were on strike and could not protect anyone.
options.misconception: No strike is mentioned; the danger is that the officers are now empowered to seize people.

options.text: The officers were empowered to act as kidnappers and slave catchers.
The officers had been ordered to leave Boston.
options.misconception: The officers had not left Boston; the warning is to avoid them because they are hunting fugitives.

rationales.A: The broadside says the opposite: the officers had become slave catchers, not abolitionists.
rationales.B: No strike is mentioned; the danger is that the officers are now empowered to seize people.
rationales.C: The broadside warns that since the mayor and aldermen's order, the police “are empowered to act as Kidnappers and Slave Catchers.”
rationales.D: The officers had not left Boston; the warning is to avoid them because they are hunting fugitives.
rationales.general:
1. Picture an ordinary Boston street, where a Black resident might stop to chat with a policeman.
2. Read what changed: the mayor and aldermen's order turned those same officers into slave catchers.
3. Follow the warning to its advice: do not converse with them, shun them, keep a sharp lookout.
Remember: a law changes more than courtrooms; it changes who is safe to talk to on the street.
